title: Arrest By J. N. L. P. Of Male Chinese Named Yau Lee Sung-Further Enquiries Re Origin Of Jacket Containing Anti-"Enemy" Slogans

page_data.en:
FM. 2
G. 20M 1 37

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No............
S.I, Special Branch XXXXX
REPORT
Date October 22. 1937.

Subject Arrest by J.M.I.P. of male Chinese named Yau Lee-sung
- Further enquiries re origin of jacket containing
anti-"Enemy" slogans.

Made by J.M.I. Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by C. [Signature]

With reference to the arrest by the J.M.I.I. of a
male Chinese named Yau Lee-sung (姚連生) at the corner of
Nining and North Kiangse Roads on the afternoon of October 21
(Hongkew Misc. 906/37), further enquiries were made of the
origin of the jacket which he wore and which contained anti-
"Enemy" propaganda.

Mr. Tong ring (董斌), a staff member of the
Lester Memorial Church refugee camp, in which Yau Lee-sung
has been living, was interviewed at his office, 137 Shantung
Road, at 5.45 p.m. October 21. He stated that about three
weeks ago, a number of cotton padded jackets were collected
at the Church premises for the benefit of Chinese soldiers
on the advice of the Shanghai Municipality Consolation Committee.
As far as he could recollect, nothing was written on the
jackets. On examining the one worn by Yau Lee-sung,
Mr. Tong recognized it as one which was considered badly
made and therefore left in the Church. He could not tell
who wrote the slogans on the lining and realized the danger
to the wearer should he fall into the hands of the Japanese.
Mr. Tong further stated that the jacket was taken away by
Yau Lee-sung without permission, but promised to see that
no such propaganda was utilised in future in the refugee
camp.

Kao Yen-ken
D. S. I.

D. C. (Special Branch).

日期：1937年10月22日。

主题：日本海军陆战队逮捕一名名为姚連生（Yau Lee-sung）的华籍男子
——进一步调查其夹克内含有反“敌”标语的来源。

由特别股督察高恩根（Kao Yen-ken）制作，经 C. [签名] 转呈

关于10月21日下午在宁兴路与江西北路转角处，日本海军情报机构（J.M.I.I.）逮捕一名名为姚連生（Yau Lee-sung）的华籍男子一事（虹口杂项案卷 906/37），对其所穿且内含反“敌”宣传品的夹克来源进行了进一步调查。

10月21日下午5时45分，在山东路137号的办公室内，对李斯特纪念堂难民收容所的工作人员董斌（Tong ring）先生进行了问询，姚連生一直居住在该收容所。董先生表示，大约三周前，根据上海市慰劳委员会的建议，教堂场所内收集了一批棉袄，以供中国士兵使用。据他回忆，这些夹克上并未书写任何文字。在检查姚連生所穿的那件夹克时，董先生认出这是一件因做工拙劣而被留在教堂的夹克。他无法说明是谁在内衬上书写了标语，并意识到若穿着者落入日本人手中将面临危险。董先生还指出，这件夹克是姚連生未经许可擅自拿走的，但他承诺今后将确保难民收容所内不再利用此类宣传品。

高恩根
特别股副督察

特别股副总监。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Arrest by J.N.L.P. of male
Chinese named Yau Lee Sung.
------------------------------------

At 3.15.p.m. on 21.10.1937 J.P.C.225 brought to station a male Chinese named Yau Lee Sung (姚連生) age 61 years, Native of Pootung, S/Carpenter, residing at Mah Kah Cheu, Foochow Road, whom he reported had been handed over to him by Japanese marines at the Chapoo Road sub station with a request that this man be passed across the Garden Bridge.

Enquiries revealed that at 12.30.p.m. on the 21.10.1937 the Chinese had walked along Haining Road from the direction of North Klangse Road and, on attempting to pass behind the Japanese barricade, had been detained and taken to the Chapoo Road sub station.

The man who appeared below normal intelligence was questioned by D.S.Guess and stated that he was a carpenter and when in Shanghai lived at Foochow Road. He had wished to visit a friend living in Hongkew District but being unable to cross the Garden Bridge had proceeded via Nantao and Chapei with a view to entering this district from North Szechuen Road. This he did but was, as stated, arrested.

名为姚連生（Yau Lee Sung）的华籍男子。
---

1937年10月21日下午3时15分，警员编号225将一名名为姚連生（姚連生）、61岁、浦东籍、职业木匠、居住在福州路马家宅（Mah Kah Cheu）的华籍男子带至巡捕房。该警员报告称，此人是由日本海军陆战队在乍浦路分巡捕房移交给他的，并要求将此人有外白渡桥移交过去。

调查显示，1937年10月21日中午12时30分，该华人从江西北路方向沿海宁路行走，在试图穿过日军路障后方时被扣留，并被带往乍浦路分巡捕房。

这名看似智力低于常人的男子接受了特别股副督察盖斯（Guess）的讯问，并称自己是木匠，在上海时居住在福州路。他本想探望一位住在虹口区的朋友，但因无法通过外白渡桥，便经由南市和闸北，试图从四川北路进入该区。他确实这样做了，但如前所述，随后被捕。

that he was wearing a black loosely tied jacked with
a white lining. On this lining were several Chinese
Characters translation of same being as follows:-

"For the preservation of the Fatherland
and freedom we must struggle with the
enemy until the bitter end".

"We will not return until we have killed
all the enemy".

Questioned regarding this jacket Yau stated that
he received this together with his other clothes from
the Lester Memorial Church, Shantung Road. Assisted by
Clerk Wong enquiries were made at this address and it
was confirmed by Mr Tong Ping (董斌) that the man was
a refugee and that the clothing including the inscribed
jacket had been given to him at the Church.

In view of the nature of the writings and the
possibility that this method might be used to circulate
propaganda the jacket and wearer were later handed over
to D.I.Ross, Special Branch, for enquiries.

Yau Lee Sung is being returned to the Lester Church
refugee centre upon conclusion of enquiries.

他身穿一件黑色系带宽松的夹克，内衬为白色。内衬上写有几个汉字，翻译如下：

“为保存祖国
与自由，我们必须与
敌人斗争到底”。

“不杀尽敌人，
誓不还乡”。

就该夹克进行讯问时，姚声称他是连同其他衣物一起从山东路的李斯特纪念堂获得的。在文员黄（Wong）的协助下，对该地址进行了查询，董斌（Tong Ping）先生证实该男子是一名难民，包括这件题字夹克在内的衣物均由教堂发放给他。

鉴于文字的性质以及这种方法可能被用于传播宣传品的可能性，该夹克及穿着者随后被移交给特别股的罗斯（Ross）督察进行调查。

调查结束后，姚連生将被送回李斯特教堂难民中心。

Whounean
高级侦探督察 10月22日。
